title: API 653 Training: Online Tank Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 653 exam prep for storage tank inspectors: self-paced online study, instructor Q&A, worked shell and floor calculations, open-book practice.
h1: API 653 Training and Exam Prep for Aboveground Storage Tank Inspectors
html:
The API 653 examination asks you to think like the inspector who signs off an in-service tank: read a thickness survey, decide whether a shell course or a corroded patch can still hold product at its fill height, judge a floor against the next interval and review a weld procedure. Below: what the exam tests, the calculations that cost the most marks, worked through, and how the self-paced course and its instructor Q&A fit around a working job.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) sets the eligibility rules, administers the API 653 examination and issues the certification. The course prepares you for it.

What the API 653 exam tests, and is it open book?

The examination has 170 questions: 140 scored and 30 unscored pretest items that look like the rest. 110 are closed-book and 60 are open-book. The day lasts about 7.5 hours: a short tutorial, 2.75 hours closed-book, a 45-minute lunch break and 3.75 hours open-book, in person at a designated Prometric test centre. You bring no papers or books; for the open-book part, PDFs of the code sections on the Publications Effectivity Sheet are on the computer.

So "is API 653 open book?" has the answer: partly. The Body of Knowledge says the closed-book part tests the working knowledge an inspector carries, and the open-book part tests detail the inspector is expected to find in the documents. Some formulas are provided, but the interval rules and the corrosion-rate and remaining-life formulas may be asked closed-book, some marked tables may be asked without the documents, and a calculation may be set in US customary or SI units. All calculations concern existing tanks, not new construction.

Who should take API 653, and eligibility in brief

API 653 is the certification for inspectors of in-service aboveground storage tanks at refineries, terminals, chemical plants and pipeline tank farms. Eligibility under Annex D combines education with tank experience gained in the last ten years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency: one year with a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology, up to five or more with no formal education. The full table is on the API 653 certification requirements page. You can study before your experience is complete, but the course does not count towards it; API decides eligibility when it reviews your application.

The API 653 Body of Knowledge and the publications examined

API publishes a Body of Knowledge and a Publications Effectivity Sheet for its exam windows. The sheet issued for the 2027 windows lists the editions below; study from the sheet for the window you book, because an addendum moves clause numbers and changes values.

Not expected: thickness for wind, earthquake or small internal pressure, nozzle loads, flanges, venting, structures, grillage-supported bottoms, brazing and the variable design point method. For recent changes, see API 653 Body of Knowledge changes explained.

API 653 calculations, with worked examples

One hypothetical tank runs through these examples: 120 ft diameter, maximum liquid level 40 ft, five 8 ft courses, specific gravity 0.9, unknown plate specification and an original joint efficiency of 1.0 on record. Practice figures only.

Allowable stress S

For the bottom and second courses S is the smaller of 0.80Y and 0.429T; above them, the smaller of 0.88Y and 0.472T. For unknown material API 653 uses Y = 30,000 psi and T = 55,000 psi, giving 23,600 psi (0.429 × 55,000, rounded) for the lower two courses and 26,000 psi (0.472 × 55,000, rounded) above. Do not use the upper value on the second course.

Whole-course minimum thickness

API 653 4.3.3.1 gives tmin = 2.6 (H − 1) D G / (S E) for an entire course, with H the height in feet from the bottom of the course to the maximum liquid level. The minus one mirrors the API 650 one-foot method. First course: tmin = 2.6 × 39 × 120 × 0.9 / 23,600 = 0.464 in.

The top course shows the rule's floor: tmin is never less than 0.1 in. for any course.

Corrosion rate and remaining life

Rate = (t previous − t actual) / years; remaining life = (t actual − t minimum) / rate. If the lowest first-course reading fell from 0.531 in. to 0.507 in. in six years, the rate is 0.004 in. per year and the remaining life (0.507 − 0.464) / 0.004 = 10.75 years. Watch for millimetre readings and nominal thicknesses offered as distractors. See long-term and short-term corrosion rates.

A locally thinned area: t1, t2 and L

For a corroded area, tmin = 2.6 H D G / (S E) at the lowest point of the area, with no minus one, and E may be 1.0 where the area is clear of welds by at least the greater of 1 in. or twice the plate thickness. A patch in the first course with its lowest point 2 ft up gives H = 38 ft:

  1. tmin = 2.6 × 38 × 120 × 0.9 / 23,600 = 0.452 in.
  2. t2, the least thickness excluding pits, is 0.400 in.; it must be at least 60% of tmin (0.271 in.), so it passes.
  3. L = 3.7 √(D × t2) = 3.7 × √48 = 25.6 in., under the 40 in. limit.
  4. Five equally spaced readings over L (0.470, 0.455, 0.448, 0.461, 0.466 in.) average t1 = 0.460 in., above 0.452 in.

Now add the corrosion allowance needed until the next inspection to both tests. At 0.003 in. per year over five years, t1 must reach 0.467 in., so the area fails for that run: shorten it, lower the fill height or repair. Stopping at step four is the trap.

Scattered pits and maximum fill height

Widely scattered pits may be ignored if none leaves less than half tmin (excluding corrosion allowance) and their dimensions along any vertical line total no more than 2 in. in an 8 in. length. Rearranging the whole-course formula gives the fill a thin course will carry: H = S E t / (2.6 D G) + 1, where t is the measured thickness less any corrosion allowance needed until the next inspection. At 0.440 in. after that deduction, the first course supports 23,600 × 0.440 / 280.8 + 1 = 37.98 ft, so about 37.9 ft rounded down. Hydrostatic test height uses the same shape with the test stress St and no specific gravity, since the medium is water. The exam provides these formulas; it tests whether you choose the right one.

Bottom plates and the critical zone

API 653 4.4.5.1 projects the floor to the next internal inspection: MRT is the lower of the remaining thickness after soil-side corrosion (RTbc) and after product-side pitting (RTip), minus the operating period Or times the sum of the unrepaired top-side rate (StPr) and the soil-side rate (UPr). With RTbc = 0.17 in., RTip = 0.19 in., StPr = 0.002 and UPr = 0.006 in. per year, a ten-year run leaves 0.17 − 10 × 0.008 = 0.09 in. The bottom tables in API 653 require 0.10 in. where there is no means of detecting and containing a leak, so ten years fails; with detection and containment the minimum is 0.05 in. and it passes. The longest run against 0.10 in. is (0.17 − 0.10) / 0.008 = 8.75 years, before the Section 6 interval rules apply.

In the critical zone, within 3 in. of the inside of the shell, the plate must keep the smaller of half its original thickness (less original corrosion allowance) or 50% of tmin of the lower shell course, never below 0.1 in., unless a stress analysis is done. For 0.25 in. plates under the example first course, that is 0.125 in. See tank floor pitting and remaining thickness.

Reconstruction, settlement and repairs

A rebuilt shell on a tank up to 200 ft in diameter is checked to the API 650 one-foot method, td = 2.6 D (H − 1) G / Sd + CA and tt = 2.6 D (H − 1) / St, with stresses from API 650 Tables 5.2a and 5.2b and API 653 8.4; the larger governs. With illustrative Sd = 20,000 psi, St = 22,500 psi and 0.0625 in. allowance, the example first course gives td = 0.610 in. and tt = 0.541 in. Settlement questions draw on Annex B (edge settlement, bottom settlement near and remote from the shell, survey points); repair questions on hot taps (9.15), replacement plates (Figure 9.1) and lap-welded patches (9.3). See what Annex B decides about settlement.

Where API 650 catches API 653 candidates

API 650 is a construction standard, but the 653 exam leans on it wherever a tank is repaired, altered or reconstructed. Expect impact-testing questions (design metal temperature, Material Group, whether testing is required, whether values pass), weld sizes for shell and roof openings, joint efficiency and the type and extent of radiography, and general welding rules in API 650 Section 9 and API 653 Section 11. Many API 650 annexes are excluded, among them D, E, F, J, K, L, P, T, V, W, X and Y. See API 650 vs API 653.

Welding and NDE: ASME Section IX and Section V

The welding procedure review gives you a WPS and its PQR and asks whether the variables are addressed and the mechanical test results acceptable. The Body of Knowledge keeps it to SMAW or GMAW, one process and one filler metal per record and P-No. 1 base metals, with no dissimilar metals, overlays, Charpy requirements, supplementary essential variables or heat treatment. A dozen practice reviews beat reading Section IX end to end.

Section V is examined in Articles 1, 2 (radiography), 6 (penetrant), 7 (magnetic particle, yoke and prod only, without T-765 and T-766) and 23, limited to SE-797 ultrasonic thickness measurement. Candidates from NDT will know much of this; candidates from engineering or operations should start it early. For hands-on method training, see ultrasonic testing training.

An API 653 study plan, phase by phase

The course is self-paced, so the plan runs by phases rather than weeks; move on when you pass the check without notes.

  1. Set up: get the Body of Knowledge, effectivity sheet and listed editions for your window, and read API 653 once through.
  2. Closed-book core: suitability for service, brittle fracture, inspection, repair, reconstruction, testing and records, with Annex B, RP 575 and the RP 571 mechanisms.
  3. Calculations: every family above in both unit systems, naming the clause each time.
  4. API 650 and welding: impact testing, opening welds, joint efficiency and procedure reviews.
  5. Exam simulation: timed papers in the real closed-book and open-book proportions, reviewed question by question.

When a thinned area crosses into the course above, when E for a patch near a weld is unclear, or when a PQR does not support a WPS range, send the question to the instructor and get the clause that settles it.

Open-book technique for API 653

  • Pace: 60 open-book questions in 3.75 hours is about 3.75 minutes each; 110 closed-book in 2.75 hours is a minute and a half.
  • Learn the map: shell evaluation in Section 4, bottom rules in 4.4, settlement in Annex B, hot taps in 9.15, reconstruction tolerances in the Section 10 tables.
  • Search the PDF in the code's words: "locally thinned" finds the corroded-area rules, "thin spot" finds nothing.
  • Write the given H, E and G down before opening a document; most open-book errors are a correct formula with a wrong input.
  • Answer every closed-book question on the first pass and flag the slow ones.

After the API 653 exam: certification and recertification

API scores the exam and issues the certificate. Certification runs three years and is ANSI-accredited under ISO 17024. Recertification opens 90 days before expiry, with a 90-day grace period and late fees, and needs at least 20% of your time in the last three years spent performing or supervising tank inspection (otherwise the full exam), plus 24 CPD hours across at least two categories. Every six years there is a 25-question open-book web quiz on code changes. See how to verify an API inspector certificate.

Sponsoring API 653 candidates as an employer

Tank owners, terminal operators and inspection contractors often sponsor several candidates at once. Each studies around rotations and turnarounds and applies to API separately, and fees are quoted on request. Atlantis also carries out remote storage tank RBI studies, and the ASNT NDT training the same crews need is under NDT training courses.

faq.q: Is the API 653 exam open book?
faq.a: Partly. Of 170 questions, 110 are closed-book and 60 open-book. In the open-book part, PDFs of the code sections on the effectivity sheet are on the test computer; you cannot bring books or notes. The interval rules and the corrosion-rate and remaining-life formulas may be asked closed-book, so memorise them.

faq.q: Do I need API 650 for the API 653 exam?
faq.a: Yes, where the Body of Knowledge names it: impact testing, opening weld sizes, joint efficiency and radiography extent, welding rules and the one-foot formulas for reconstructed shells. Many API 650 annexes are excluded, so use it as the reference behind repair and reconstruction questions, not as a design course.

Corrosion rate and remaining life, shell tmin for whole courses and thinned areas, pitting, fill height, bottom remaining thickness, settlement, hot taps, patch plates and API 650 impact testing. The API 653 shell minimum thickness guide covers the shell rules in depth.

faq.q: Are formulas provided in the API 653 exam?
faq.a: Some. The Body of Knowledge says the fill-height formulas and the bottom operating-period formulas are provided, while the interval rules and the rate and remaining-life formulas may be asked closed-book. Know the shell tmin, rate and life formulas well enough to use them without looking.

faq.q: Does the course include API 653 practice questions?
faq.a: Yes: original questions with explanations, calculation drills and timed papers in the 110 closed-book and 60 open-book split. They are written for practice and are not questions from the API examination. Each explanation names the clause or table that decides the answer, so you also learn where it sits.

faq.q: Is the variable design point method on the API 653 exam?
faq.a: No. The Body of Knowledge lists it with wind, earthquake and internal pressure thickness, nozzle loads, flanges, venting and grillage-supported bottoms among calculations candidates are not expected to perform. Spend that time on the one-foot formulas, corroded areas and the bottom.

faq.q: Can an employer enrol a group of tank inspectors?
faq.a: Yes. Employers can sponsor several candidates, each studying at their own pace with access to the instructor. Every candidate still applies to API individually and must meet the eligibility rules in their own right. Tell us how many people and which window, and we will send the details and a quote.

faq.q: Is API 579 on the API 653 exam?
faq.a: No. API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 is not among the publications on the 2027 effectivity sheet. The exam is set on API 653, API 650, RP 571, 575, 576, 577, 651 and 652 and ASME Sections V and IX, within the limits the Body of Knowledge sets.
